newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota's February output falls due to fire.
newsitem.headline: Toyota's February output falls due to fire.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp. said Friday its output fell 13 percent in February because of a fire at a parts supplier, but rivals Honda and Nissan both reported jumps in production.
Honda Motor Co. Ltd and Nissan Motor Co. Ltd said the increased production was due to a boost in exports, helped by a weaker yen.
Toyota said its output fell 13.5 percent because a fire on Feb. 1 at a brake parts supplier forced it to idle all of its domestic plants.
All the major carmakers except Toyota reported increased exports in February, which analysts said should continue into the fiscal year starting from April 1.

"Japan's exports in the year to March 1998 are likely to go up by 2 to 3 percent from 1996/97, partly helped by the weak yen and increased shipments to the Middle East, Africa, and some models to Europe and niche models to the United States," said Nobuaki Yanachi, Kankaku Research senior analyst.
While Toyota's exports fell 17.5 percent in February to just under 90,000 vehicles, export increases for the other carmakers ranged from 3.0 percent for Mazda to a booming 37.2 percent for Honda.
Industry sources said the increases meant that exports for the full year to March 31 would probably increase for the first time in five years, industry sources said.
The boost in car exports has helped increase Japan's trade surplus, especially with the United States.
Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus rose 6.5 percent in February from a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen ($5.58 billion), the first rise in over two years, the Finance Ministry said on March 17.
Toyota's February output fell to 269,695 vehicles while its exports dropped to 89,282 units.

Nissan's output jumped almost 10 percent to 159,653, and its exports rose 18.1 percent to 53,579. Honda's production was up 19.9 percent to 107,418 vehicles while exports climbed 37.2 percent to 43,650.

Mazda's production fell 3.3 percent to 75,824 vehicles but exports rose 3.0 percent to 47,689. Mitsubishi Motors Corp.'s output nudged down 0.9 percent to 116,519, but exports rose 5.9 percent to 46,770.
